title: Net Exchange piece 8: audit the clear-out, finish it, write the panel list
purpose: Close piece 8 ("remove what is left of the old shell") of the one-panel screen rebuild of the Net Exchange currency-exchange bureau application. When the result of this call has been applied by hand and has passed the owner's local checks, (1) the web code holds no leftover of the old page shell, (2) section 2 of docs/spec.md is the list of panels exactly as the code has them, tied to the routes by a test, and (3) README.md, app/README.md and the plan document say what is true. The result is reviewed line by line and applied on the owner's machine by another agent, called "the terminal" below. It must therefore be exact, as small as the task allows, and honest about everything that was not run.
task: Work only from the supplied files, in this order. (1) Unpack netexchange-snapshot.zip twice, as base/ and as work/, and change only work/. The snapshot is git commit 31212a2 of branch main plus the uncommitted change shown in piece8-clearout.diff, which is already applied in the snapshot; the snapshot's root folder netexchange/ is the repository root. (2) Audit that change (R1, R2). (3) Search the web code for further leftovers of the old page shell and remove what is proven dead (R3). (4) Add the two test files (R4, R5). (5) Rewrite section 2 of docs/spec.md as the list of panels (R6, R7, R8), noting on the way where documents and code differ (R17). (6) Bring README.md and app/README.md up to date (R9, R10) and append the block of piece 8 to the plan (R11). (7) Run what your environment can run and record it word for word (R12, R13). (8) Produce the patch with a diff tool, the changed files in full, the report and the main JSON (R14, R15, R16, R18). Words used in this job: a PANEL is the one card in the middle of the screen, the JSX element <Panel> of app/src/web/panel.tsx; the CASHIER is the person at the counter (role "operator"); an ADMINISTRATOR has the role "admin"; an ADDRESS is the path and query of the URL; a KEY is a numbered thing pressed as Ctrl with its number and shown in a small cap (PickKey in app/src/web/panel.tsx); the STAGE ROW is the row of names on the top line that says where the cashier is (where() in app/src/web/flows.ts); the OLD SHELL, or the PAGES OF BEFORE, is the page frame of the application before the rebuild (a page title, tabs, tables), which pieces 1 to 7 replaced screen by screen; the OWNER is Sina, who decides.

The screen rebuild has nine pieces. Pieces 1 to 7 are built and committed: every screen is a panel. Piece 8 is this call. The owner's rule of the keys, as built in app/src/web/keys.ts and app/src/web/panel.tsx: everything on a panel has a key and shows it in a cap, a box as well as a button; a numbered thing is pressed with Ctrl and its number from anywhere, also from inside a box; a number never moves while its panel is up, so a thing that is away keeps its place (KEPT); a panel has at most ten keys, 1 to 9 and then 0; Enter goes on; Esc goes back; Ctrl with Enter goes on from a box of several lines; Ctrl with the left arrow puts the cursor in the rates list and Ctrl with the up arrow in the top line.

requirements.requirement: SECTION 2.2, THE PANELS. The table has the header '| Panel | Address | For | What it asks or shows | Keys |' and one row per panel. WHAT A ROW IS: a panel is a state of the screen with its own title or question. List in results.panels every <Panel element in app/src/web outside tutorial, with file and line. Elements that draw the same title for the same purpose (a loading or an error state of one panel) share a row; an element whose title depends on a state (for example a title that says 'Add to' in one state and 'Take from' in another) gets one row for each state. Add a row for every screen drawn without <Panel: check app/src/web/pages/Login.tsx (the sign-in) and app/src/web/pages/Receipt.tsx. ORDER OF THE ROWS: the sign-in; Home; First steps; the panel behind a currency and Rate history; then the choices of Home in the order of HOME in app/src/web/flows.ts, each with its panels in the order a cashier meets them (a deal's panel and the receipt belong to Find a deal); under Business the choices in the order of BUSINESS; under Set up the choices in the order of SET_UP. THE CELLS. Panel: the title or question as the cashier reads it, in double quotes, a variable part in capitals ("What do you want to do with CODE?"), followed in parentheses by the name the stage row gives the panel when that differs. Address: in backticks, the route path as App.tsx writes it, with ':panel', ':statement', ':name' and ':group' written out as their values, one row per value, exactly as R5 expands them, and ':id' and ':code' left as written; then, still inside the backticks, the query that selects this panel when it has one (for example `/team?new=1`, `/kiosk?branch=ID&show=pending`), a variable value in capitals; when the panel is a state of that address with no address of its own, the word (view) after the closing backtick. The sign-in row has (signed out) and no backticks. For: 'everyone', 'administrator', or the condition in a few words, read from the guards of the routes in App.tsx, from SET_UP and setUpFor in flows.ts and from the panel's own code. What it asks or shows: one or two sentences in the screen's own words saying what is read there and what is decided there; name the note 'How this is calculated' where the panel has one. Keys: every numbered thing in the order of its number, as '1 name, 2 name', with the words its cap stands beside; '0' is the tenth key; a place held for a thing that is away is written '(4 held for NAME)'; a run of list rows is written '2–7 the rows'; then what Enter does and where Esc leads, a few words each; 'none' where nothing is numbered. The numbers are read from the usePicks or numberPicks call of that panel; results.panels gives its file and line as keys_source. What differs by role is said in the cell (for example 'a cashier has 1 only'). No two rows have the same Panel cell: where two panels carry the same title, the later one is told apart by words in parentheses (for example the name of its flow). One <Panel element can be drawn at several addresses (the panels an exchange and a transfer share): it then has a row for each address, and its entry in results.panels names all of them in spec_rows.
